name: online_delete rotation interval
measurement: Rotation tips: S1 [1256, 1512], S6 [1301, 1601, 1901, 2157], S10 [1311, 1567]. Each rotation fired at the first close where the interval, can_delete, and health gates all held, and lastRotated jumped to that tip — so a rotation delayed by can_delete (S6: first at 1301, not 1256) shifts the next interval. S1 deleted 1255 rows in 13 batches of <=100; S10 deleted 1310 rows after the deferral. Effectiveness: 100% — every rotation fired exactly when the gate allowed it.

name: can_delete advisory gate
measurement: can_delete steps: never -> ok=0; {'hash_seq': 1200} -> ok=1200; now -> ok=1301; always -> ok=4294967295. Cumulative rotations after each following validate block: [0, 1, 2, 4]. 'never' held rotations at 0 for 300 ledgers; the hash of 1200 authorised up to 1200 (1 rotation, at tip 1301); 'now' set can_delete to lastRotated 1301, which satisfies can_delete >= lastRotated - 1, so it authorised exactly 1 more rotation (at tip 1601); 'always' released the rest (4 total rotations). Effectiveness: 100% — 4/4 argument forms behaved as documented.

name: shouldAcquire window gate
measurement: Backfill halts: S3 at 1743 (gate-refused; 2000-1743=257 > 256, below minimumOnline 1744), S4 at 1257 (fetch-failed; the floor ledger itself, which no peer holds), S5 at 1256 (gate-refused; 2000-1256=744 > 256, below minimumOnline 1257). Acquired before the halt: S3 0, S4 742, S5 743. Effectiveness: 100% — the gate refused exactly where the rule says it must, and S4's halt is a peer failure, not a gate error.

name: minimumOnline floor
measurement: S3: with no online-delete floor, minimumOnline is the SQL minimum (1744 at halt time), so the backfill stops at the 256 window (halt 1743). S4/S5: with online delete on, minimumOnline is the stored floor (1257), so the backfill descends past the window to the floor (S4 halt 1257 on a fetch failure, S5 halt 1256 on the gate). Effectiveness: 100% — the floor is honoured as coded in both forms.

name: clampFetchDepth
measurement: S9 part 1: fetch_depth 1000000000 clamped to 256 (online_delete), earliest fetch 1744. Part 2: fetch_depth 100 clamped to 100, earliest fetch 1900. Effectiveness: 100% — both clamps match min(fetch_depth, online_delete).

name: hashOfSeq skip-list resolution + candidate ledger
measurement: S2: 4 requests failed at the candidate step (reference ledger 1024 not held, peer lacks it), 2 resolved the hash through the held candidate 1280 and then failed on the target acquire, 1 failed on a direct hash acquire; S3: 15/15 deep requests resolved through an acquired candidate (1536, then 1024). Effectiveness: 100% — the candidate path behaved as coded in every case.

name: InboundLedger timeout model (6 x 3000 ms)
measurement: S2: 28 timeouts over 7 failed acquires — 7 each for the 4 first attempts; the 3 repeats of the failed candidate hash (1024) short-circuited via mRecentFailures with 0 timeouts (84000 ms total acquire time). S7: 7 timeouts for the failed clean of 1000 (first acquire attempt 7; the retry short-circuited). Effectiveness: 100% — the timeout model fired exactly as coded, including the failure cache.

name: fetch-pack earliest-fetch gate
measurement: S9: 2 fetch-pack roots refused as 'too early' (1744 and 1800 after the clamp to 100), 5 served, 2 refused because the node does not hold the ledger. Effectiveness: 100% — the gate refused exactly the roots below getEarliestFetch.

name: LedgerCleaner repair
measurement: S7: 3/4 ledgers cleaned. 1500 recovered from the peer, 1600 re-saved after an SQL mismatch, 1700 was already clean; 1000 failed because no peer holds it and was dropped from the complete set. Effectiveness: 100% as coded when a peer holds the ledger (3/3), 0% when none does (0/1) — the control cannot repair what no peer holds.

name: RPC validated-age gate
measurement: S8 at validated age 121 s: index request -> rpcNOT_SYNCED; hash request -> served (seq 1999); v1 index request -> rpcNO_CURRENT. Effectiveness: 50% coverage — the gate fires for ledger_index (1/1) and is bypassed by ledger_hash (0/1), which has no age check in the pinned code.

name: RPC index bounds and exactly-one rule
measurement: S8: index 2000 -> 'Ledger index too large', index 0 -> 'Ledger index too small', both fields set -> param_error. Effectiveness: 100%% — 3/3 parameter errors fired before any fetch was attempted.

name: doAdvance history backfill
measurement: Backfill acquired: S3 0, S4 742, S5 743 ledgers. S3 and S5 halted on a shouldAcquire refusal (S3 at 1743, S5 at 1256); S4 halted on a fetch failure at 1257 after the peer refused the floor ledger. Effectiveness: 100% — the history branch acquires exactly the ledgers the gate allows, no more.

name: tryFill contiguous marking
measurement: S4 final complete ledgers 1258-2000; S5 final complete ledgers 1257-2000. Effectiveness: 100% — tryFill marked exactly the contiguous acquired ranges complete.

name: LedgerHistory SQL fallback
measurement: S1: ledgers 1256 and 1257 (below the skip-list window) served from SQL rows. S2: 1300, 1400, 1500 served from SQL. Effectiveness: 100%% — every in-window SQL lookup succeeded (5/5).

name: clearSql batched delete (batch 100)
measurement: S1: 1255 rows in 13 batches (10 + 3, batch 100). S6: 1900 rows in 20 batches. Effectiveness: 100% — no batch exceeded 100 rows.

name: rotation health gate (age <= 60 s, FULL mode)
measurement: S10: 0 rotations across 300 stale ledgers (age 61 s) and 10 syncing ledgers; 2 rotations after the node returned to FULL with age 0 s. Effectiveness: 100% — the health gate deferred rotation exactly while the node was unhealthy.

measurement: UNMEASURED — code-verified only. The refusal fires only for a HISTORY/CONSENSUS acquire while the node needs a network ledger; no scenario set that state, so the refusal never ran. Source: InboundLedgers.cpp:70-125.

name: getLedgerBySeq SQL fallback (loadByIndex)
measurement: S9: roots 1000 and 1500 resolved to no ledger through both the skip list and the SQL fallback (refused, 'we don't have'); roots 1744, 1900, 2000 resolved. Effectiveness: 100%% — the fallback found every held ledger and reported every missing one.
